outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail, not discordant: both completed evaluations report compile_failed, solution_passed false, and 0/986 tests run. The parallel run differs from serial because it never started implementation or delegation after a provider 429. The serial run made substantial ordinary task progress, including CLI probing, asset generation, and Rust source creation, but chose external Cargo dependencies and reached cargo check only to fail on crates.io DNS in the no-network environment before another provider 429 ended the turn.
parallel_contributors: Immediate provider 429 prevented any local investigation, code creation, verification, or child-agent use.
Protocol validation reports zero spawn calls, zero child threads, and parallel_used false, so no parallel coordination episode occurred.
serial_contributors: Serial identified the target behavior and created a Rust project with source and generated assets.
Serial depended on external crates without a lockfile/vendor source and did not complete a successful build before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's dependency-based Rust implementation could not compile in the no-network environment because cargo attempted to update crates.io.
Parallel had no implementation artifact beyond the original workspace contents.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluations stopped at compile_failed, so no behavioral tests were run.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process contrast is directly evidenced but not a parallel coordination failure
